Without prejudice, the Petitioner, while having claimed payment from the Respondent as early as January 2016, chose not to file any petition until the passing of the Order by this Commission on 4.1.2024 in Petition No. 145/MP/2021 involving another generator. It is well settled that the mere fact that relief has been granted to a similarly placed person does not entitle a party that has chosen not to agitate its rights by taking recourse to appropriate legal proceedings to such relief. It also does not serve to exclude the time that has started to run from the time that the cause of action arose. (i) The present Petition was filed in August 2024, whereas the events of Change in Law for which the Petitioner claims compensation occurred in September 2021. For the period during which the Petitioner chose not to approach this Commission, the Petitioner cannot claim carrying costs, as there has been significant delay and laches on the part of the Petitioner in approaching the Commission. The principle that a delay in filing a Petition or providing information shall result in the denial of carrying cost has been established by the APTEL in several judgments. Therefore, the claim for carrying cost is not admissible if claims are not brought before the Commission promptly after events become known. (c) The contention of Respondent No. 1 as regards the claims/reliefs claimed in the Petition being barred by limitation is erroneous, untenable, and misconceived.
